arxiv-1806-01078.title: Reproducible research using biomodels Journal: Bulletin of Mathematical Biology
arxiv-1806-01078.creator: Pedro Mendes
arxiv-1806-01078.description: Abstract Like other types of computational research, modeling and simulation of biological processes (biomodels) is still largely communicated without sufficient detail to allow independent reproduction of results. But reproducibility in this area of research could easily be achieved by making use of existing resources, such as supplying models in standard formats and depositing code, models, and results in public repositories.

arxiv-2011-08836.title: Improving the estimation of environment parameters via initial probe-environment correlations
arxiv-2011-08836.creator: Hamza Ather, Adam Zaman Chaudhry
arxiv-2011-08836.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Hamza Ather, Adam Zaman Chaudhry. Small, controllable quantum systems, known as quantum probes, have been proposed to estimate various parameters characterizing complex systems such as the environments of quantum systems. These probes, prepared in some initial state, are allowed to interact with their environment, and subsequent measurements reveal information about different quantities characterizing the environment such as the system-environment coupling strength, the cutoff frequency, and the temperature. These estimates have generally been made by considering only the way that the probe undergoes decoherence.

arxiv-2110-11980.title: Multipartitioning topological phases by vertex states and quantum entanglement
arxiv-2110-11980.creator: Yuhan Liu, Ramanjit Sohal, Jonah Kudler-Flam, Shinsei Ryu
arxiv-2110-11980.description: Abstract We discuss multipartitions of the gapped ground states of (2+1)-dimensional topological liquids into three (or more) spatial regions that are adjacent to each other and meet at points. By considering the reduced density matrix obtained by tracing over a subset of the regions, we compute various correlation measures, such as entanglement negativity, reflected entropy, and associated spectra.

arxiv-2111-04459.title: Triple-level Model Inferred Collaborative Network Architecture for Video Deraining
arxiv-2111-04459.creator: Pan Mu, Zhu Liu, Yaohua Liu, Risheng Liu, Xin Fan
arxiv-2111-04459.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pan Mu, Zhu Liu, Yaohua Liu, Risheng Liu, Xin Fan. Video deraining is an important issue for outdoor vision systems and has been investigated extensively. However, designing optimal architectures by the aggregating model formation and data distribution is a challenging task for video deraining. In this paper, we develop a model-guided triple-level optimization framework to deduce network architecture with cooperating optimization and auto-searching mechanism, named Triple-level Model Inferred Cooperating Searching (TMICS), for dealing with various video rain circumstances.

arxiv-2408-14008.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qihang Ge, Wei Sun, Yu Zhang, Yunhao Li, Zhongpeng Ji, Fengyu Sun. The explosive growth of videos on streaming media platforms has underscored the urgent need for effective video quality assessment (VQA) algorithms to monitor and perceptually optimize the quality of streaming videos. However, VQA remains an extremely challenging task due to the diverse video content and the complex spatial and temporal distortions, thus necessitating more advanced methods to address these issues.

arxiv-2507-11023.creator: Jeremy Mould, and Adam Batten
arxiv-2507-11023.description: Abstract We explore the consequences of a novel but increasingly well-supported hypothesis that supermassive black holes may have formed from primordial black holes formed prior to, and rapidly growing in, the radiation-dominated universe. We show that this hypothesis can predict the luminosity of quasars and their luminosity distribution.

pmc-13237374.title: Rapid elongation drives the exceptionally fast aggregation of the most common localized human amyloid medin
pmc-13237374.creator: Vaidehi Roy Chowdhury, Robert I Horne, Mariana P Cali, Zenon Toprakcioglu, Sara Linse, Michele Vendruscolo
pmc-13237374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Amyloid deposition is a hallmark of numerous age-related diseases, and understanding the chemical mechanisms that govern amyloid formation is crucial for advancing the rational development of protein aggregation inhibitors. With amyloid formation rates varying widely across proteins, here we report the quantitative aggregation mechanism of medin, the most common localized amyloid in humans, and find it to be much faster compared to well-known pathological amyloids such as amyloid-β (Aβ), tau and α-synuclein.

pmc-13570778.title: Orthobiologics in anterior cruciate ligament injuries
pmc-13570778.creator: Marc Daniel Bouchard, José Leonardo Rocha De Faria, Gustavo Vinagre, Douglas Mello Pavão, Nelson Merchan, Emmanouil Papakostas, Gilbert Moatshe, Pedro Bernáldez Domínguez, Theodorakys Marín Fermín, Ignacio Dallo, Ashraf Hantouly
pmc-13570778.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury remains a major challenge in sports medicine because it affects a young and active population and is associated with instability, secondary meniscal and chondral damage, delayed return to sport and post‐traumatic osteoarthritis. This narrative review provides an ACL‐specific overview of orthobiologics, with an emphasis on the biologic rationale, current clinical applications and the strength of the available evidence.

pmc-13571306.title: Protocol for modeling biliary cell activation in human precision-cut liver slices
pmc-13571306.creator: Beatrice Anfuso, Manuela Mastronardi, Silvia Palmisano, Giovanni Sorrentino
pmc-13571306.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPersistent ductular reaction is a hallmark of chronic liver injury, characterized by the proliferation and pro-inflammatory activity of reactive biliary epithelial cells. Here, we present a protocol for modeling biliary cell activation in human precision-cut liver slices. We describe steps for collecting samples, generating, and culturing precision-cut liver slices, and activating biliary cells ex vivo while preserving native architecture and multicellular interactions.
